To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) TAA ions do not form aggregates in solution; (2) the average water orientation around the cations is tangential; (3) the dynamics in the CoM motion of the cations is very similar to that of the bulk solution; (4) water dynamics is slowed down relative to bulk water; and (5) the slowing down of the water dynamics is not as large as might be expected.
the dynamics of water in concentrated aqueous solution of TAA cation is slower than in bulk water.

the tetraalkyl ammonium cations do not form aggregates in aqueous solutions, even at high concentration, they are penetratable for water and anions, and their global rotation slows down with concentration.

the TAA cations are not aggregated in aqueous solution, and the dynamics of the ions and solvent are not strongly coupled, which is in contrast with simple alkali cation systems, such as Na+.
the hydrophobic TAA cations are penetrable for water and the water structure around them is similar to that of bulk.

the dynamics of TAA cations in aqueous solutions are very similar to those of simple alkali cation, despite the fact that TAA cation has a very hydrophobic character.
